name: Hong Kong
tagline: The world's cheapest Michelin-starred pork bun, and the first Chinese restaurant to reach three stars.

Lung King Heen.description: The world's first Chinese restaurant to earn three Michelin stars, a specialist in luxury dim sum. Reviewed by critic Amanda Sheppard for the South China Morning Post.

Tim Ho Wan.description: The world's cheapest Michelin-starred restaurant. Its baked barbecue pork bun is legendary, and Anthony Bourdain ate here on 'Parts Unknown'.

Luk Yu Tea House.description: A classic tea house since the 1930s, with original Art Deco decor.

Yat Lok.description: Michelin-starred roast goose in a simple cha chaan teng-style spot in Central, with more than 20 secret preparation steps.

Australia Dairy Company.description: An iconic Kowloon cha chaan teng, famous for its scrambled eggs and no-nonsense fast service.

Bo Innovation.description: Chef Alvin Leung's two-Michelin-starred 'X-treme' Chinese cuisine. Anthony Bourdain visited the restaurant on the Hong Kong episode of 'No Reservations'.

Amber.description: Three-Michelin-starred French fine dining at the Landmark Mandarin Oriental, led by chef Richard Ekkebus.

The Chairman.description: One-Michelin-star Cantonese restaurant that topped Asia's 50 Best Restaurants in 2021, sourcing ingredients from local farms and fishermen.

Duddell's.description: Michelin-starred Cantonese restaurant set inside a 1920s-style art collector's mansion on historic Duddell Street.

T'ang Court.description: Luxury Cantonese restaurant at the Langham Hotel in Tsim Sha Tsui, holding three Michelin stars for over a decade.

Forum Restaurant.description: Three-Michelin-star temple of abalone founded in 1977 by Yeung Koon-yat, the 'Abalone King,' who once served his signature dish to Deng Xiaoping.

Ming Court.description: Two-Michelin-star Cantonese restaurant at the Cordis (formerly Langham Place) in Mong Kok, led by chef Mango Tsang.

Fook Lam Moon.description: Known as the 'tycoons' canteen,' this classic Wan Chai Cantonese institution since 1948 is a favorite of Hong Kong's business and political elite.

Yung Kee.description: Wellington Street institution since 1942, famed for its charcoal roast goose, with over 80 years of family history.

Ho Lee Fook.description: Contemporary Cantonese restaurant in Soho Central, with a casual atmosphere and cooking by chef ArChan Chan.

Spring Deer.description: Peking restaurant open since 1969 in Tsim Sha Tsui, celebrated for its honey-glazed roast duck.

Lin Heung Tea House.description: Century-old tea house in Central serving dim sum the traditional way, with trolleys wheeled around the dining room, since 1926.

One Dim Sum.description: Unassuming Prince Edward spot serving Michelin-quality dim sum at bargain prices; earned a Michelin star in 2011-2012.

Joy Hing Roasted Meat.description: Char siu and roast meat shop dating to the late Qing dynasty in Wan Chai, recognized with a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Sister Wah.description: Clear-broth beef brisket specialist in Tin Hau, holding a Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2014.

Under Bridge Spicy Crab.description: Causeway Bay restaurant famous for its 'typhoon shelter'-style spicy crab, a Hong Kong late-night classic.

Mak's Noodle.description: Shrimp wonton noodles with a recipe dating to pre-war Guangzhou; its fame has drawn diners including Anthony Bourdain.

Tsim Chai Kee.description: Wonton noodle shop with a Michelin Bib Gourmand every year since 2009, facing rival Mak's Noodle on Wellington Street; nicknamed the 'ping pong wonton' shop for its oversized dumplings.

Ho Hung Kee.description: The first wonton noodle shop to earn a Michelin star, serving congee and wonton mee since the 1940s.

Kau Kee.description: Beef brisket noodles on Gough Street for over 90 years; TV host Andrew Zimmern said it would be his only meal in Hong Kong. Holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Sang Kee Congee Shop.description: Fish-belly congee specialist in Sheung Wan since the late 1960s, named by CNN among Hong Kong's must-eat dishes.

Tung Po Kitchen.description: Raucous North Point dai pai dong that hosted Anthony Bourdain's final filmed dinner in the last episode of 'Parts Unknown' (2018), shot alongside cinematographer Christopher Doyle.

Mido Cafe.description: A 1950 cha chaan teng in Yau Ma Tei with original stained glass and tiles; one of Hong Kong's oldest surviving traditional cafes.

Kam Wah Cafe.description: Prince Edward bakery-cafe famed for its pineapple bun (bolo bao) with butter, a Hong Kong breakfast classic.

Sing Heung Yuen.description: Central dai pai dong famous for its tomato noodle soup and crispy toast with honey and lemon.

Lee Keung Kee North Point Egg Waffle.description: North Point egg waffle (gai daan zai) stall, mentioned in the 2017 Michelin Guide Hong Kong & Macau.

Hui Lau Shan.description: Dessert chain founded in the 1960s in Yuen Long, pioneer of the mango sago dessert it popularized in 1992.

Yee Shun Milk Company.description: Causeway Bay specialist in 'double-skin' steamed milk pudding, with a recipe imported from Macau.

Tai Cheong Bakery.description: A 1954 bakery on Lyndhurst Terrace famous for its cookie-crust egg tarts, the favorite of former governor Chris Patten.

Kee Wah Bakery.description: Traditional Chinese bakery founded in 1938 in Kowloon, celebrated for its mooncakes and bridal pastries.

Quinary.description: Hollywood Road cocktail bar that pioneered 'multisensory mixology,' a regular on Asia's 50 Best Bars list.

The Old Man.description: Ernest Hemingway-inspired Central bar, ranked among the World's 50 Best Bars.

Graham Street Market.description: Hong Kong's oldest street market, with over 160 years of history in the heart of Central.

Cheung Hing Kee Shanghai Pan-Fried Buns.description: Sheng jian bao (soup-filled pan-fried buns) specialist with a Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2016.

Tsui Wah Restaurant.description: Cha chaan teng chain founded in 1962, the first of its kind to list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange; its Lan Kwai Fong branch is a post-clubbing classic.
